keyVerseText: And if thy right eye offend thee, pluck it out, and cast it from thee: for it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not that thy whole body should be cast into hell. offend: or, do cause thee to offend
rootMeaning: The Greek noun μέλος (mélos) primarily denotes a 'member' or 'limb' of the body, emphasizing a part that is integral to the whole organism. While its exact etymology is uncertain, its core sense centers on a physical component or segment of a living body, which metaphorically extends to parts of a collective entity. This literal sense enriches the English gloss by highlighting not just any part, but a vital, functioning segment that contributes to the unity and operation of the body as a whole.
usageInScripture: Across its 34 occurrences, μέλος is most frequently translated as 'members' (21 times) or 'member' (7 times), consistently referring to parts of a body or figurative parts of a collective, such as the church or the body of Christ. The word appears in both singular and plural forms, often emphasizing the interconnectedness of individual parts within a greater whole. This usage reveals a consistent metaphor of unity and diversity within the body, whether physical or spiritual, underscoring the importance of each part's role and function.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding μέλος as a 'member' or 'limb' deepens our grasp of the biblical metaphor of the church as the body of Christ, where each believer is a necessary and purposeful part. This imagery teaches that no Christian is isolated or insignificant; each has a unique role that contributes to the health and mission of the whole. The word's original meaning as a physical limb reminds us that spiritual unity requires diversity and interdependence, reflecting Christ's design for the church. It also calls believers to holiness and vigilance, as seen in its application to the body and its members, urging the removal of anything that causes spiritual harm.
keyVerseReflection: Matthew 5:29 warns, 'And if thy right eye offend thee, pluck it out, and cast it from thee,' illustrating the serious call to remove anything that causes sin. Here, the word μέλος ('members') highlights that even a single part of the body is worth sacrificing to preserve the whole. This stresses the value and impact of each member, and the necessity of holiness in every part of our being to avoid eternal loss. The metaphor powerfully communicates the cost and urgency of spiritual purity within the Christian life.
